scope: Theorem 5.1 (Positive-law alternative) of the manuscript “Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture” (preprints/Koebes-Circle-Domain-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 071 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0080bd36e38b2cd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 32-33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that, for some β > 0, there is no new compatible barrier coordinate with ∥du∥2,G\O + ∥au∥ℓ2(B) < β. 32 Nonexistence here allows an arbitrary countable enlargement of the flags and, in the gated problem, any penalty region permitted in Definition 4.1. Then there is a probability law µ on base codes with the following properties: (i) ℓ̄µ = gµ da, where gµ ∈ L2(G, da); (ii) nµ|D∗ ∈ ℓ2(D∗) and mµ ∈ ℓ2(B); (iii) for every slot and every tag type, its tuple distribution, regarded as a subprobability measure, is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on the corresponding tuple torus. The three norms in (i)–(ii) are bounded by a constant depending only on β and the numerical constant in Theorem 4.3. In particular, the bound does not depend on any auxiliary countable subset of B or any auxiliary finite atomless measure on B.
